sessions.topic: Core Communication Protocols, Analytical Tools, and Live Packet Interception Practicals
sessions.notes:
Resumed the Network Security Fundamentals module covering Category 2 and Category 3 glossary terms. Explained the security implications of unencrypted protocols (HTTP/Telnet) versus encrypted protocols (HTTPS/SSH) using practical analogies. Guided the students through two live Kali Linux practicals. Students successfully launched Wireshark with root privileges, captured baseline traffic on the eth0 interface, and used display filters to isolate HTTP POST requests and extract cleartext credentials.

Action Items:
1. Students must complete the Take-Home Assignment (answering questions 1 through 7).
2. Save the assignment as a PDF and upload it to the course portal before the next scheduled class.
3. Retain the recorded PCAP files from today's exercises for future forensic review.

sessions.topic: Network Architecture, Addressing (MAC vs. IP), Transport Mechanics (TCP/UDP), and Protocol Security
sessions.notes:
Student demonstrated strong comprehension during today's deep dive into network security fundamentals and protocol mechanics. We analyzed data packetization and evaluated physical vs. logical addressing—distinguishing MAC addresses as permanent hardware fingerprints and IP addresses as temporary network locations.

We broke down core communication concepts using practical scenarios:
1. DNS operations on Port 53 mapping domain names to IP addresses.
2. Connection-oriented TCP (guaranteed delivery) vs. connectionless UDP (high-speed transmission).
3. The security risks of unencrypted transit over HTTP (Port 80 cleartext) versus encrypted transit over HTTPS (Port 443 SSL/TLS).
4. Baseline traffic monitoring fundamentals to prepare for packet analysis.

Action Items:
1. Review all Category 1 terms in the Network Protocols Glossary (IP, MAC, DNS, TCP, UDP).
2. Complete Part 1 (Port & Protocol Mapping) and Part 2 (Scenario Analysis) of the Take-Home Assignment.
3. Verify local Wireshark installation and promiscuous mode settings ahead of our cleartext credential extraction practical.

sessions.topic: Network Architecture, Protocol Analysis, and Baseline Traffic Capture
sessions.notes: Covered physical vs. logical addressing (MAC vs IP), transport protocols (TCP vs UDP), and essential Linux network commands. Guided the student through booting Kali Linux in VMware, launching Wireshark with administrative privileges, and capturing live baseline network traffic on the eth0 interface.

lmsModules.title: Module 1: Enterprise Web Architecture & Modern Frontend
lmsModules.description: Master TypeScript, modern component architecture, state machines, and responsive layouts.

lessons.title: 1.1 Deep Dive: TypeScript Generics & Strict Typing Systems
lessons.contentMarkdown:
### Learning Objectives
- Master TypeScript strict compilation flags and type narrowing.
- Implement reusable generic interfaces for enterprise REST and GraphQL consumers.
- Build type-safe schemas using Zod and TypeScript AST validation.

#### Architectural Checklist
1. Never use `any` in production APIs. Use `unknown` and discriminant unions.
2. Structure custom utility types using conditional types (`T extends U ? X : Y`).
3. Maintain immutable state representations in client applications.

lessons.title: 1.2 State Architecture: TanStack Query & Optimistic Mutations
lessons.contentMarkdown:
### Enterprise State Management Patterns
Managing server cache versus transient client UI state is the cornerstone of responsive web applications.

#### Key Principles
- **Server Cache**: Keep data cached with automatic invalidation and background refetching.
- **Optimistic UI**: Mutate local state immediately, then revert gracefully if network or business validation fails.
- **Deduplication**: Prevent redundant roundtrips across deeply nested component hierarchies.

lessons.title: 1.3 Hands-On Lab: Build an Accessible Interactive Dashboard Table
lessons.contentMarkdown:
### Lab Deliverables
You will build a full-featured data table component featuring:
- Server-side pagination and debounce searching
- Keyboard navigation (WCAG 2.2 AA compliant)
- Dynamic column sorting and export to CSV

Submit your GitHub repository link and deployed Vercel/Netlify staging URL below.

lmsModules.title: Module 2: Scalable Backend Services & API Security
lmsModules.description: Design robust microservices with Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, and secure auth tokens.

lessons.title: 2.1 Relational Schema Modeling & Query Optimization in PostgreSQL
lessons.contentMarkdown:
### Database Engineering in Fintech & Edtech
Learn normalization (3NF), B-tree indexing strategies, foreign key cascades, and ACID transactions.

lessons.title: 2.2 Payment Gateway Integration: Paystack API & Webhook Verification
lessons.contentMarkdown:
### Production Payment Processing
Integrate Paystack Inline and Webhooks to handle card payments, bank transfers, and automated commission payouts.

#### Security Requirements
- Compute and verify HMAC SHA512 signatures using your secret key.
- Guarantee idempotent transaction processing to avoid double-crediting.
- Mask sensitive transaction metadata.

lmsModules.title: Module 3: Cloud Deployment, Docker & DevOps Automation
lmsModules.description: Deploy resilient containerized workloads to Linux VPS instances with Nginx reverse proxies and SSL certificates.

lessons.title: 3.1 Containerization with Docker & Multi-Stage Production Builds
lessons.contentMarkdown:
### Containerizing Full-Stack Applications
Learn to write lean Dockerfiles, leverage caching layers, configure non-root user execution, and spin up multi-container compositions with Docker Compose.

lessons.title: 3.2 Capstone Project Submission & Mentor Defense
lessons.contentMarkdown:
### Capstone Project Defense
Submit your production-ready SaaS application featuring real-time authentication, database persistence, payment integration, and cloud deployment. Your assigned mentor will review and schedule your 1-on-1 defense session.
